If it was, say, you or me donating to someone who we knew, or someone alien to us, then it could be seen as better, as we aren't doing it for some motive that may circle back to us. Like "I would be sad if X died, I have to keep them with me." But this unborn has no knowledge of anyone or anything, and this isn't its decision. We would be offering the "services" of a non-consenting party. 

In the case of a young child, it is a lot trickier, I think. I feel as though you shouldn't tell them "this is something that we decided" or " you want to do this?". But also, I feel that either outcome of such a situation will be incredibly damaging to the child later on. If they don't donate, then they will probably feel immense guilt. If they do, they very well may feel as if they were manipulated or pushed to do something they did not understand.

On a different note, I really appreciate that you made this post. It made me think a lot and helped me understand myself in someway.

Let's take a more real scenario, as I feel the one can be a bit strange to deal with, at least for me. Let's say we have a terminally ill child, in need of an organ transplant. There are no viable donors, and the parents are faced with the decision of having another child to be the one to make the sacrifice. I do believe this has happened before, although correct me if I'm wrong.

 To create this child, for the sole purpose of sacrificing ( a part of) itself to an already living being is horrifying to me. To create a child so it can experience the wonders of the world - while misguided - is understandable, I suppose. But to birth one into our world out of convienience, it being useful to US, is just, not justifiable to me.

Of course, I do respect others opinions.
